title: `retiredFromLoadPath: true` does not keep a conversion off any load path — three runtime seams replay every retired entry with `includeRetired: true`, and `apply.ts` says only `migrate meta` does
body:
Measured on `origin/main` `c5ea982d97` while executing the ruling on #16693 (which removed the one conversion where this was actively destructive). The mechanism it removed is still there and still contradicts its own recorded contract, so it is filed separately rather than widened into that PR.

⛔ Not proposing a fix. Which arm gives — the flag's meaning, or the seams that override it — turns on what `#12772` and `#3903` bought, and both are recorded decisions.

⚠️ **Correction, same day, by the author.** The first version of this body said "78 of the 90 registered conversions carry `retiredFromLoadPath: true`". Both numbers were wrong: 78 came from a naive `grep -c "retiredFromLoadPath: true"`, which also counts four PROSE mentions of the flag inside docblocks, and 90 was read off the branch that had already removed one entry. Corrected below and re-counted as a property.

## The contract, quoted from the tree

`packages/spec/src/conversions/apply.ts:66-70`:

> ```ts
> for (const conversion of ALL_CONVERSIONS) {
>   // A retired entry is graduated chain history (ADR-0087 D2 window, second
>   // half): the loader no longer accepts its old shape — only `migrate meta`
>   // (and the fixture CI) replays it, via `includeRetired`.
>   if (conversion.retiredFromLoadPath && !includeRetired) continue;
> ```

Every retired conversion's own docblock says the same thing in its own words. The sharpest is the one #16693 removed, because it argued the flag was load-BEARING and not decorative:

> `retiredFromLoadPath` is load-bearing here in a way it is not for renames: a rename is idempotent on canonical input, but this is a DEFAULT FLIP … a loader that auto-applied this transform would stamp NOT NULL onto it, silently restoring the tri-binding the ADR removed. Only `os migrate meta --from <16 or lower>` may apply it, where "this source predates the split" is a fact, not a guess.

`.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md` teaches the same rule to every future retirement author, and `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` prints "Migration-chain-only (retired from the load path)" beside each entry.

**On `c5ea982d97`: 74 of the 91 registered conversions carry `retiredFromLoadPath: true`** — counted as an object property (`/^\s{2}retiredFromLoadPath: true,$/`), against 91 `id:` properties. After #16693's PR the same counts read 73 of 90.

## The measurement: `migrate meta` is not the only replayer, and it is not even one of these

Every `includeRetired: true` in non-test source on that tree — `git grep -n "includeRetired" -- '*.ts' ':!*.test.ts'`:

| call site | what it is | is it `migrate meta`? |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `packages/metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.ts:291` | the artifact-ingestion door, at BOOT | no |
| `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts:3536` | flow rehydration, at RUNTIME | no |
| `packages/spec/src/conversions/stored.ts:75` | `applyConversionsToStoredItem` — every stored-row rehydration seam | no |

`os migrate meta` reaches the chain through the ADR-0087 ledger, not through any of these three.

Each of the three has its own recorded rationale for opening the window, and each one is coherent read alone — `stored.ts` because a row at rest has no author for a tombstone to teach (ADR-0087 addendum), `engine.ts` for the same reason on flows (#3903), and the artifact door because a built artifact is data at rest with a version stamp (#12772). What none of them reconciles is the flag's own claim that they do not exist.

### Probe and controls, run against built `dist/` on `c5ea982d97`

Subject: an artifact declaring `engines.protocol: ^17.0.0` — the range `create-objectstack` stamps — on a 17.3.0 runtime, carrying one `required: true` field and nothing else.

```
runtime @objectstack/spec version = 17.3.0

[SUBJECT  floor ^17.0.0] verdict           = converted-forward
[SUBJECT  floor ^17.0.0] notices           = ["field-required-notnull-explicit"]   <- a RETIRED entry
[SUBJECT  floor ^17.0.0] storage.notNull   = true                                  <- and it was APPLIED

[NEG CTRL floor ^99.0.0] verdict           = authored-current                       <- window shut
[NEG CTRL floor ^99.0.0] notices           = []
[NEG CTRL floor ^99.0.0] storage.notNull   = undefined

[POS CTRL other conv   ] verdict           = converted-forward                      <- window open, different entry
[POS CTRL other conv   ] notices           = ["action-inert-keys-removed"]

[applyConversions includeRetired=false] notices=[] storage.notNull=undefined        <- the flag WORKS when not overridden
[applyConversions includeRetired=true ] notices=["field-required-notnull-explicit"] storage.notNull=true
```

The negative control proves the instrument can answer "no"; the positive control proves the window is open independently of the entry under test; the `includeRetired=false` leg proves the flag itself is not broken — it is **overridden**, wholesale, by the caller.

## Why this is worth a card now that #16693's conversion is gone

The override is harmless for the 73 retired entries that remain **today**, and for most of them it is the point: they are lossless deletes of inert keys, and replaying them at the artifact door is exactly what #12772 was filed to get.

It is not harmless for the class the flag was written for. A conversion whose old and new shapes are both LEGAL and mean DIFFERENT things — a default flip, not a rename — is applied by these three seams to sources that deliberately chose the new default, silently restoring semantics an ADR removed. That is not hypothetical: it is what #16693 measured, on a source authored in September 2026 that got the pre-split treatment purely because its dependency range reads `^17.0.0`.

Removing that one conversion removed today's instance. The next author who reads the checklist in `spec-property-retirement`, sets `retiredFromLoadPath: true` on a default flip, and believes the flag means what it says, will re-create it.

## What a reader cannot tell from the tree today

- ⛔ Whether any of the three seams INTENDED to include default flips, or only lossless deletes. `stored.ts` and `engine.ts` both argue from "data at rest has no author to teach", which is an argument about tombstones, not about default flips.
- ⛔ Whether the artifact door's floor key (declared `engines.protocol`, not artifact age) was understood to make every permissive-range app a "pre-split source". #16693's reporter measured that it does; #12772's own text keys on the declared floor deliberately.
- ⛔ Whether any of the remaining 73 entries is a default flip rather than a lossless delete. Not audited here, and that audit is the first thing a fix would need.

## Dedup

`retiredFromLoadPath` returns no issue in this repo, open or closed. Semantically nearest and NOT this: #12772 (built the artifact door and chose `includeRetired: true` — it is the record that makes this card legible) · #12844 and #14397 (other readers of the same bytes that BYPASS the door) · #16693 (the one destructive instance, ruled and removed) · #3903 (the flow-rehydration seam).
